rationale: This qualitative public-administration case study analyzes the Sabar Shouchagar ('Toilets for Everyone') initiative in Nadia District, West Bengal, India. Two governance mechanisms are co-equally central (`multiple`): (1) `institutional_structure_coordination`, via multi-agency fiscal and administrative convergence across MGNREGA, NRLM, Nirmal Bharat Abhiyan, Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan, ICDS, Block Development Officers, and elected Gram Panchayats organized into 6,620 catchment areas; and (2) `participation_assistance`, via CLTS-style community mobilization, women's self-help groups operating 107 rural sanitary marts, NGOs/faith-based groups, and village-level Para Najardari (Neighborhood Monitoring) volunteer committees. Outcomes are likewise co-equally split (`multiple`) between physical household/institutional toilet construction and coverage (`primary_connection`, increasing coverage from 60% to 97% across 336,000+ families) and sustained functional toilet adoption/elimination of open defecation (`effective_access`, increasing usage from 57% to 99.8%).
